H6TN01537.name: Kristi Burke
H6TN01537.bio: Artist who ran a mural business and has worked in the beauty industry and as a YouTube creator.

positions.stance: "Healthcare is a human right"; supports a universal, single-payer Medicare for All system so coverage never depends on employment or ability to pay.
"Public education must be fully funded"; says public dollars must go to public schools, opposing diversion of taxpayer funds through private school vouchers.
Says "the tax burden must shift off working people and onto corporations and the ultra-wealthy."
Supports hospitals, school districts, roads, internet connectivity, and water and sewage systems for rural areas whose local tax base can't support adequate infrastructure.
"Social Security is a lifeline" that must be protected from cuts and strengthened for future generations.

H8TN02119.name: Tim Burchett
H8TN02119.bio: Former Knox County mayor and Tennessee state legislator who previously ran a mulch company.

positions.stance: Says lawmakers trading stocks on non-public information is "dirty, corrupt, and wrong"; introduced the End Congressional Stock Trading Act.
Says veterans are hamstrung by VA red tape and bureaucracy and "should have the choice to get care wherever they choose."
Has pledged to support term limits legislation, saying "You can't clean up Washington with dirty career politicians."
Supports a Balanced Budget Amendment and opposes raising taxes, saying the federal government "already taxes and spends too much."
Calls Israel "our single greatest ally" and supports its right to defend itself and an undivided Jerusalem as its capital.

H6TN02170.name: Michaela Barnett
H6TN02170.bio: Civil engineering PhD who built a small business in Knox County and worked in Congress as a science policy fellow.

positions.stance: Supports legislation that backs "workers, families, and innovation, not just the already-wealthy," saying working hard should get you ahead.
Says quality health care "should be affordable and accessible to everyone who needs it," measured by patients healed rather than profit.
Says elected officials are "bought off by corporate interests" and pledges to fight corruption and fix what's broken in government.
Says infrastructure has not kept up with growth and pledges to bring federal tax dollars home to invest in the region.
Lists a plan to "invest in our education" among her key priorities.

H0TN03254.name: Chuck Fleischmann
H0TN03254.bio: U.S. Representative for Tennessee's 3rd District and member of the House Appropriations Committee; former small business owner.

positions.stance: Committed to "getting government out of the way," supporting business investment, lower taxes, and reduced regulatory burdens.
Supports a constitutional amendment prohibiting the federal government from spending more than it collects each year.
Wants to continue overhauling the tax code so taxpayers keep more of their money; "he'll keep fighting to lower taxes."
Strongly opposes amnesty and says immigration reform "begins with building the wall on our southern border."
Pledges to "always fight to preserve our conservative values" and constitutional rights he says are under attack.

H6TN03228.name: Anna Golladay
H6TN03228.bio: Owner of Biased Apparel, CEO of consulting firm Work of Place, and former associate pastor in Chattanooga.

positions.stance: Supports wages that cover the bills, "the freedom to organize and bargain collectively," and small businesses that can compete.
Says rural communities need "fully funded hospitals, strong schools, reliable infrastructure, and a representative who shows up year-round."
Says Oak Ridge's federal investment should serve community, science, and environment: "We can fund our labs and protect our land."
Says "Health care is a human right" and criticizes Tennessee's refusal to expand Medicaid amid rural hospital closures.
Supports "protecting reproductive freedom, defending LGBTQ+ lives, and honoring the sacred worth of every single person."

H0TN04195.name: Scott DesJarlais
H0TN04195.bio: Physician and U.S. Representative for Tennessee's 4th District; member of the House Armed Services and Agriculture committees.

positions.stance: "A firm supporter of an amendment to the Constitution that would require a balanced budget each year."
Says the economy works best when people keep more of their money and "government gets out of the way."
Supports tax reductions and simplification for middle-class Americans and job creators, and fewer burdensome regulations on farmers and small businesses.
Opposes ObamaCare; favors interstate insurance competition, tort reform, and incentives for health savings accounts.
Supports a strong national defense and resources for service members: "Our military must always be a top priority of the Congress."

H4TN04270.name: Victoria Broderick
H4TN04270.bio: Lincoln County resident and former county party chair who also ran for this seat in 2024.

positions.stance: Plans to "close the coverage gap & keep rural hospitals open."
Pledges to "protect responsible gun owners and reduce gun violence."
Calls for "real oversight on war and defense spending."
Supports "voluntary Pre-K for every child."
Plans to "create a path to homeownership for working Tennesseans."

H6TN05405.name: Charlie Hatcher
H6TN05405.bio: Farmer, veterinarian and business owner; former Tennessee State Veterinarian and Commissioner of Agriculture.

positions.stance: Will fight inflationary federal spending and unnecessary regulations, and supports expanding American energy production so families keep more of what they earn.
Says "Food security is national security"; will fight to protect farmers, strengthen agricultural biosecurity, and reduce dependence on foreign food.
Supports enforcing immigration laws and giving Border Patrol the resources needed, while maintaining a legal immigration system for those who follow the rules.
Supports an all-of-the-above energy strategy including natural gas, nuclear, and renewables, and fewer regulatory and permitting delays.
Believes hostile foreign governments and adversary-controlled entities should not be allowed to buy American farmland.

H6TN05397.name: Chaz Molder
H6TN05397.bio: Mayor of Columbia, Tennessee, first elected in 2018.

positions.stance: Will advocate for "a ban on stock trading by members of Congress" to restore trust in government.
Pledges to champion affordability by lowering healthcare, housing, and grocery costs, and to strengthen workers' right to organize and labor protections.
Committed to lower healthcare costs and support for rural hospitals; supports expanding insurance coverage and investing in preventive services.

H6TN06171.name: Mike Croley
H6TN06171.bio: Navy veteran and engineer; former TVA efficiency engineer and Presidential Management Fellow at NOAA and the Departments of State and Agriculture.

positions.stance: His AAA Blueprint lists ending "Trump's reckless tariffs," taxing the rich fairly, building affordable housing, and making unionization easier to lower costs.
Lists making voting more accessible, improving veterans' healthcare access, expanding the House, and restricting insurers' ability to deny claims.
Lists releasing the unredacted Epstein files, scaling back DHS and ICE funding, banning congressional stock trading, and term limits for Congress.

H6TN06213.name: Johnny Garrett
H6TN06213.bio: Tennessee State Representative and House Majority Whip; attorney in Sumner County.

positions.stance: Committed to working with President Trump to pass "his America First agenda" in the U.S. House.
Supports a physical border wall and President Trump's use of the military and Guantanamo Bay to deport illegal immigrant criminals.
Supports "keeping men out of women's sports, and especially out of their locker rooms."
Believes "if Tennessee families and the State have to balance their budget, the federal government should too."
Will fight to make the 2017 tax cuts permanent and expand them; "We shouldn't tax social security, tips or overtime."

H6TN07161.name: Matt Van Epps
H6TN07161.bio: West Point graduate and Army Special Operations combat pilot; former Commissioner in Governor Bill Lee's administration.

positions.stance: Will partner with President Trump to bring manufacturing back, unleash American energy, and pass legislation to regulate and unleash crypto and AI innovation.
Will work to reform the VA, eliminate red tape, and ensure veterans get the healthcare, benefits, and support they've earned.
Supports "finishing the wall, empowering Border Patrol," and ending what he calls the left's open-border agenda.
Will fight overregulation and foreign land grabs, defend property rights, and push to expand rural healthcare.
"Fully committed to advancing President Trump's America First agenda," including cutting waste and reining in spending.

H6TN07286.name: Darden Copeland
H6TN07286.bio: Founder and CEO of the Calvert Street Group, a Nashville public affairs firm; former campaign manager and political strategist.

positions.stance: Will fight to protect Medicaid, defend affordable premiums, lower prescription drug costs, and keep rural hospitals open.
Supports a full ban on stock trading by members of Congress, their families, and the Executive Branch, and supports term limits.
Calls them earned benefits and pledges "no cuts, no privatization, no games" with seniors' retirement security.
Says he "will not be a rubber stamp for any president or party" and will stand up to Donald Trump.
Will take on price gouging, expand affordable housing, cap prescription drug prices, and make child care affordable.

H2TN07103.name: David Kustoff
H2TN07103.bio: Former U.S. Attorney for the Western District of Tennessee and member of Congress.

positions.stance: Calls community and national safety his "top priority," citing his record fighting public corruption, violent crime, and drugs as U.S. Attorney.
Says "Local folks know best"; opposes national mandates and Common Core, and supports public schools.
Says the government's first priority is national security; supports fully funding the military and says "We must always support Israel."
Supports funding the border wall and stopping illegal immigration and drug trafficking, while backing legal immigration for those who play by the rules.
Believes life begins at conception, marriage is between a man and a woman, and in an "unequivocal constitutional right to keep and bear arms."

H6TN08367.name: Heidi Kuhn
H6TN08367.bio: Shelby County Criminal Court Clerk with more than two decades in government roles.

positions.stance: Pledges to repeal cuts to SNAP benefits that provide food assistance to working-class Tennesseans.
Will expand the Child Tax Credit to make raising children more affordable.
Will expand the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit and stand up to Wall Street investors buying up housing and raising rents.
Will oppose monopolistic grocery chain mergers and fight "shrinkflation."
Will lower utility bills by investing in American energy production and cracking down on price gouging by big energy companies.

H6TN09449.name: Justin Pearson
H6TN09449.bio: Tennessee State Representative from Memphis, elected in 2023.

positions.stance: Supports a federal jobs guarantee, a true living minimum wage, making billionaires and corporations pay their fair share, and passing the PRO Act.
Supports passing Medicare for All and investing in rural hospitals and the VA healthcare system.
Supports permits to carry, a ban on assault rifles, and background checks and cooling-off periods for firearm purchases.
Supports fully funding public education and reining in "voucher scams."
Supports pausing hyperscale data center construction until comprehensive health, environmental, and economic protections pass.

H6TN09464.name: Brent Taylor
H6TN09464.bio: West Tennessee State Senator and funeral home business owner; former Memphis City Council member and Shelby County Election Commission chairman.

positions.stance: Says he "stands proudly with President Trump and the America First agenda."
Will champion priorities including finishing the border wall, deporting criminal illegal immigrants, cutting spending, eliminating DEI mandates, and defending parental rights.
Will fight to lower the cost of living by cutting federal spending and regulations, citing his state law making data centers pay power infrastructure costs.
Will promote expanded domestic oil, natural gas, and nuclear power to lower costs and improve national security.
Will cut wasteful programs, oppose bloated omnibus bills, and restore accountability so families keep more of what they earn.

H0IN01150.name: Frank Mrvan
H0IN01150.bio: U.S. Representative for Northwest Indiana serving his third term; former North Township Trustee for 15 years.

positions.stance: Supported the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law and has delivered federal Community Project Funding to grow the Northwest Indiana economy.
Committed to bipartisan solutions to lower the cost of living; supports investments in wind, solar, and hydrogen to increase affordable energy supply.
Supports banning all stock trading by Members of Congress, "because public servants are elected to serve – not get rich."
Supports the PRO Act, expanded Buy America requirements, Davis-Bacon wage requirements, and Project Labor Agreements.
Says women's access to reproductive healthcare is under attack after Roe v. Wade was overturned.

H6IN01231.name: Barb Regnitz
H6IN01231.bio: Porter County Commissioner; former United Airlines software engineer and project manager and Certified Financial Planner.

positions.stance: Wants criminals arrested, prosecuted, and held accountable, an end to catch-and-release policies, and support for law enforcement.
Supports stronger border security against illegal crossings, drugs, and trafficking, and immigration policies prioritizing "safety, legal entry, and accountability."
Supports ending reckless spending, curbing inflation, eliminating waste, fraud, and abuse, and reducing the national debt.
Supports same-day, in-person voting with watermarked paper ballots and limiting mail-in ballots to "rare, verified exceptions."
Wants schools to teach "students how to think, not what to think" and to keep girls' sports and facilities for biological females.

H2IN02295.name: Rudy Yakym
H2IN02295.bio: U.S. Representative for Indiana's Second District.

positions.stance: States an "unwavering commitment to limited government, individual liberty, and fiscal responsibility."
Aims to "cut through the red tape, dismantle unnecessary regulations, and streamline government agencies."
Wants to restore the balance between federal and state powers, "allowing for greater local control and decision-making."

H6IN02189.name: Jamee Decio
H6IN02189.bio: Attorney and former Elkhart County deputy prosecutor.

positions.stance: Says "Your tax dollars should be working for you, not for Wall Street," criticizing corporate handouts as Hoosiers are priced out of homes.
Supports universal healthcare "working alongside private payers" to help small businesses, save taxpayers money, and improve quality of life.
Says the U.S. is "a nation built and sustained by immigrants" and should live up to the values it preaches.
Says technology should improve communities and support workers, never serving as "a tool for corporate exploitation" that burdens working families.
Says the President and members of Congress "must be beyond reproach" and constitutional violations must be answered.

H0IN03198.name: Marlin Stutzman
H0IN03198.bio: Fourth-generation farmer and business owner from Howe, Indiana; former Indiana state legislator elected to the U.S. House in 2010.

positions.stance: Blames out-of-control spending and a broken tax system for inflation and says the tax system must be fixed so workers can succeed.
"Finish the Wall"; says "We cannot have a secure nation without secure borders."
Says "Education was never meant to be a federal issue" and is the responsibility of parents first, working with states and communities.
Authored the Bureau Guidance Transparency Act demanding complete transparency from federal agencies.
Lists "Defending the Unborn" as an issue, citing years of marching for reversal of the 1973 decision legalizing abortion.
Promises to "Make Indiana Affordable Again" by lowering costs on housing, healthcare, education, utilities and energy.
Promises to "Fight for Medicare for All."
Promises to fully fund education "from child care to college by taxing Wall Street."
Promises to "End U.S. wars in the Middle East and bring our troops home."
Promises to "Put Hoosiers first, not corporations and foreign governments."

H6IN04193.name: Drew Cox
H6IN04193.bio: Marine Corps veteran with a doctorate in music who helps on his family's farm in Henry County.

positions.stance: Supports "a single-payer medicare for all healthcare system."
Pushing to overturn Citizens United and get big money out of politics.
Will fight to protect the freedom of the American people and civil rights, keeping the state within constitutional limits.
Committed to a pro-worker agenda to raise the minimum wage, support unions, and battle poverty.
Says government must respect autonomy in decisions about "our bodies and our personal relationships."

H0IN05326.name: Victoria Spartz
H0IN05326.bio: CPA, finance executive, and business owner; former CFO at the Indiana Attorney General's Office and adjunct faculty at IU's Kelley School of Business.

positions.stance: Supports limited government, preserving Second Amendment freedoms, and protecting "the sanctity of all human life."
Says the debt is unsustainable; supports cutting spending, welfare reform, and a balanced budget without raising taxes.
Supports fixing a slow, costly legal immigration process and "a more robust work visa program" to curb illegal immigration.
Supports keeping the military strong and providing better services to veterans.
Supports more transparency, competition, consumer choice, and "value-based, not volume-based" health care delivery models.
Will "always fight for full transparency on data centers," including disclosure of expected utility and water usage before construction.
Supports banning international investors and big corporations from buying homes, controlling utility costs, opposing Trump's tariffs, and lowering health care costs.
Pledges regular town halls, opposes corporate tax breaks for unwanted projects, and supports protecting Social Security benefits and constitutional rights.
Will fight to restore and protect Medicaid funding, oppose cuts to emergency and preventive care, and keep rural hospitals open.
Lists "Make Life Affordable" first among his issues.
Lists "Secure the border" among his issues.
Lists "Cut Government Spending" among his issues.
Lists "Back the blue" among his issues.
Lists "Support America's Troops" among his issues.

H6IN06230.name: Cynthia Wirth
H6IN06230.bio: Former biology and environmental science teacher at Columbus Signature Academy and community business owner for more than 20 years.

positions.stance: Will work for good-paying jobs, affordable housing and childcare, and equal access to benefits like sick time and paid family leave.
Will support the professional teacher workforce and ensure neighborhood preK-12 schools are safe and welcoming for all students.
Will fight for accessible and affordable healthcare for all Hoosiers, saying health "should never be a commodity traded to make profit."
Will push for clean energy investments and says "no" to data centers that consume extreme amounts of fossil fuels, water and electricity.

H8IN07184.name: André Carson
H8IN07184.bio: U.S. Representative for Indiana's 7th District; former Indianapolis City-County Council member and law enforcement officer.

positions.stance: Supports investing in early childhood education, equitable K-12 resources, raising teacher salaries, and expanding Pell Grants.
Committed to fighting Trump's tariffs and supporting policies that strengthen "the middle class – not the ultra-wealthy."
Opposes SNAP cuts and introduced the Food Deserts Act to fund grocery stores in underserved communities.
Supports a strong military, NATO and other alliances, defending democracy and human rights, and investing in diplomacy and humanitarian aid.
Supports protecting Medicare and Medicaid and addressing health disparities, including Black maternal health and community health center access.
